newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Rough seas bar repair of key Taiwan oil port.
newsitem.headline: Rough seas bar repair of key Taiwan oil port.

text.p: State-owned Chinese Petroleum said on Wednesday strong currents were preventing repairs to its only north Taiwan crude port and that it could not say when oil would flow again to a nearby refinery.

A company executive also confirmed to Reuters that Chinese Petroleum's purchase on Wednesday of 32,000 tonnes of jet fuel was necessitated in part by a partial shutdown of the Taoyuan refinery, which makes aircraft fuel.
"Chinese Petroleum's repair team is still trying to fix problems in the two oil offloading units that have been shut down, but strong currents stopped us," he said by telephone.
The tanker Vanadis, carrying about 300,000 tonnes of African crude, remained anchored nearby for a fourth day.
The official said the Vanadis could soon be redirected to the company's southern crude port at Kaohsiung for offloading.

The oil giant shut down the offshore units at the weekend due to unspecified pipeline problems, cutting off the flow of crude to the Taoyuan refinery, which in turn was forced to shut down one of its two distillation units to slow production.

The Chinese Petroleum official did not comment on reports from Singapore that it may be considering a second purchase of jet oil but confirmed that the Taoyuan slowdown was a factor in Wednesday's purchase at tender.
"We did put the shutdown into consideration for the purchase of jet fuel on Wednesday," the official said.
Chinese Petroleum, a state monopoly that dominates jet fuel sales in Taiwan, cancelled one of Wednesday's two jet oil tenders due to high offering prices.
